Quick answer: This guide compares 6 alternatives to Microsoft Word, with prices copied from each official website. Free options: Google Docs, LibreOffice Writer, Zoho Writer and WPS Office Writer. Paid plans start at $3.50 (Google Docs). For comparison, Microsoft Word itself costs $5.40/month. Use the table below to match price and free plan to your budget.

Last checked: November 17, 2026. Based on each tool's official website and pricing pages. Prices and features change, so confirm details on the official site before you buy. How prices are checked | Report a mistake

Freelancers and small teams often evaluate Microsoft Word alternatives 2026 because of the ongoing subscription costs and platform preferences. Paying for document software requires careful thought when free options exist. I examine the official pricing and features to help you decide.

At a glance facts from official pages:

  • Pricing model: Free plans, open-source options, and subscriptions starting from $3.50 up to $14.
  • Platforms: Web, Windows, macOS, Linux, iOS, and Android depending on the tool.
  • Best for: Real-time collaboration, heavy book writing, and general office tasks.

Exploring Microsoft Word alternatives

Google Docs

Google Docs is an online document and PDF editor designed for real-time collaboration. It allows you to create online documents and edit PDFs from any device. The software includes AI to generate drafts and templates. It features a free plan with paid options starting from $3.50.

LibreOffice Writer

LibreOffice Writer is a free and private office suite with no forced AI. It operates as a desktop application for your writing needs. The software is completely open-source and available at no cost. You can download it without paying any subscription fees.

Zoho Writer

Zoho Writer is an online word processor designed for smooth teamwork and collaborative writing. It supports Windows, macOS, Linux, iOS, Android, and Web platforms. The editor includes Zia, a free AI-driven writing assistant built into the system. It is listed as a free edition.

WPS Office Writer

WPS Office Writer is free word processing software that helps you create and edit documents. It runs on Windows, Mac, Linux, Android, iOS, iPad, and Web platforms. The software includes AI-powered tools to translate, summarize, and polish text. It is advertised as free forever.

Scrivener

Scrivener is a dedicated novel and book writing software for authors and long-form creators. It combines tools to organize, edit, and craft your first draft. The software supports Windows, macOS, and iOS platforms. It costs US$14 and offers a free trial.

Notion

Notion is an AI workspace where teams can capture knowledge and find answers instantly. It brings multiple systems of record into one unified platform for small businesses and startups. The platform features a free plan with paid tiers starting from $8/month.

Pros and cons of the tested options

  • ✅ Google Docs offers real-time collaboration across multiple devices.
  • ❌ Google Docs lacks explicit free trial details on its main page.
  • ✅ LibreOffice Writer is completely free and open-source with no forced AI.
  • ❌ LibreOffice Writer does not list a native mobile platform in the provided text.
  • ✅ Zoho Writer includes multi-column layouts and a free AI assistant named Zia.
  • ❌ Zoho Writer pricing beyond the free edition requires verification.
  • ✅ WPS Office Writer runs across nearly all major desktop and mobile platforms.
  • ❌ WPS Office Writer premium limits are not fully detailed in the snippet.
  • ✅ Scrivener provides specialized organization tools for long-form book writing.
  • ❌ Scrivener costs US$14 and only supports specific operating systems.
  • ✅ Notion acts as a comprehensive workspace with built-in AI agents.
  • ❌ Notion paid plans start at $8/month which may add up for large teams.

Who should stay with Microsoft Word

You should stay with Microsoft Word if your workflow relies heavily on advanced formatting and the specific AI suggestions provided by Copilot. Freelancers who collaborate with clients demanding native DOCX compatibility will find the official ecosystem hard to replace. When evaluating tools, some professionals also research Remote Gaze and Discord alternatives to understand broader software pricing models. Sticking with Microsoft Word makes sense if you already utilize its bundled family plans or personal subscriptions ranging from free online tiers to paid plans starting at $5.40/month.

Always verify platform compatibility and offline access requirements before committing to a paid writing application for your freelance business.

Frequently asked questions

Is Microsoft Word free to use?

Yes, Microsoft Word offers a free online version for document editing. Paid plans start from $5.40/month if you need advanced features and desktop applications.

Which alternative is best for writing books?

Scrivener is specifically designed as novel and book writing software for creators. It costs US$14 and includes a free trial for Windows, macOS, and iOS.

Are there completely free word processors?

Yes, LibreOffice Writer is a free and open-source office suite with no forced AI. Zoho Writer and WPS Office Writer also provide free editions for users.
